newsitem.title: USA: Palomar previously filed suit against MEHL.
newsitem.headline: Palomar previously filed suit against MEHL.

text.p: Palomar Medical Technologies Inc on Wednesday said it had filed a declaratory judgement suit against MEHL/Biophile International Corp months before MEHL accused Palomar of patent infringement.

Palomar said it filed "several months ago" in Boston District Court, a lawsuit in seeking a declaration that Palomar's Epilaser hair removal system does not infringe on MEHL/Biophile's hair removal method. It also sought to show that MEHL's patent is both invalid and unenforceable.
MEHL/Biophile said on Monday that its Selvac Acquisition Corp unit filed a patent infringement suit against Palomar seeking to halt Palomar from marketing its laser hair removal products in the U.S.

On Tuesday, Palomar said it had received U.S. Food and Drug Administration to sell and market its Epilaser system, and that it has been granted a U.S. patent for their hair removal technology. They also said they hold a an exclusive global license for the technology.

"We filed this declaratory judgment months ago after learning that MEHL/Biophile was misrepresenting to our customers that our product might infrnge on their patent," said Steven Georgiev, chairman and chief executive of Palomar in a statement.
"We are announcing our lawsuit today since our patent was only issued recently and, therefore, all of the information is now in the public domain, allowing for resolution of these issues," he said.
